task.title: Page pending due one-shot schedules sparsely
task.objective: Complete issue https://github.com/Knosence9/project-vela/issues/1001 with bounded exact-ID scan pages filtered to pending schedules due by a caller-owned cutoff.
acceptance_criteria: Inspect at most one positive at-most-1024 authoritative schedule window plus lookahead and return complete pending schedules due at or before the inclusive cutoff.
Preserve exact-ID scan order and advance continuation from the last inspected schedule across nonmatching windows.
Fail closed on selected or lookahead corruption while keeping complete due-instant-ordered discovery behavior unchanged.

outcome.summary: Issue 1001 delivered storage-work-bounded pending-due paging without adding indexed schema, clocks, or lifecycle authority.

verification.command: GitHub Rust quality gate for pull request 1002 exact head adb7b51f93cb8cff6817f0c59560f387a9ec0e83

lessons: A dense due-result page cannot honestly bound work when future or non-pending schedules may be arbitrarily sparse.
Exact-ID scan order provides bounded fail-closed paging but intentionally differs from complete list_due ordering by due instant then ID.
Arbitrary u64 due instants in JSON payloads require a separate indexed-schema and migration decision before due-instant keyset paging.
The boundary reads no clock and adds no persisted cursor, claim, materialization, dispatch, permission, or execution authority.
